subject: SIG/CAIQ field canonicalization + S3 presign upload workflow
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@acme-soft.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/CAIQ field canonicalization + S3 presign upload workflow

Hi Julia —

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday to run through the Whistic profile. We ran into two small but annoying gaps when we tried a CSV import: duplicated fields ("App Name" vs "Service Name") and a handful of SIG/CAIQ QIDs that are mapped to non-canonical keys in your export.

To keep the onboarding moving I sketched a minimal proposal attached: a canonicalization map that maps your exported field ids -> Redwood canonical names, plus a short S3 presign upload playbook for evidence files. High level asks:
- Can your team accept a single CSV that uses the canonical column names (see attached redwood_whistic_field_map_v1.csv)?
- For evidence we prefer a short-lived S3 presign workflow (we provide presigns and you upload). See s3-presign-playbook.md attached for entitlements and TTL.

If presigns aren’t an option, we can also accept a password-protected ZIP via your portal but that adds manual steps.

Proposed next steps (quick):
1) You confirm you can accept the canonical CSV columns OR tell us the exact field ids we should target.
2) If presign is OK, reply with the email to put on the upload ACL and we’ll send a batch of presigns (24h TTL).
3) We’ll stage a one-hour import window Thursday morning to ensure no collisions.

Thanks — goal is to keep the profile import atomic so we don’t create duplicate fields that confuse annual SIG pulls.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Security Ops | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: redwood_whistic_field_map_v1.csv (csv), s3-presign-playbook.md (text)

From: Julia Park <julia@acme-soft.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-soft.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ field canonicalization + S3 presign upload workflow

Hi Soojin —

Appreciate the clear plan and the attachments. A couple quick clarifications from our end:

- We can accept a CSV with canonical column headers but our export uses internal field ids (e.g. fld_1072) and we typically need a mapping file. Your CSV looks like it does that — good.
- Presign uploads are generally OK but two constraints: (1) our legal team requires evidence uploads to be restricted to accounts tied to the contract (so we need the uploader email to match john.doe@acme-soft.com), and (2) TTL cannot exceed 48 hours.

Before we proceed please:
- Send a small sample mapping (3 rows) with actual sample values so our import script can do a dry-run.
- Confirm the presign TTL and whether uploads can be scoped to a single prefix (we prefer per-customer prefixes).

I can loop in John from procurement if needed, but for now security@acme-soft.com will observe the transfer.

On timing — Thursday morning works, but we prefer starting at 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Vendor Risk Manager | Acme Software
julia@acme-soft.com

Quick internal note —

We can accommodate their constraints but a couple guardrails from our compliance side:
- Presign TTL: 24 hours preferred, 48 hours max (we should log presign generation and TTL in the import ticket).
- Upload ACL: we can restrict to a single uploader email for the prefix (john.doe@acme-soft.com) but we must ensure we capture an assertion of upload possession (signed manifest) — I recommend the presign playbook include a tiny manifest.json that the uploader POSTs into the same prefix after upload (filename: manifest_signed.json) with an SHA256 list and who-uploaded field.
- Field mapping: ask them for the sample 3-row dry-run and we will run import in a staging workspace. If any fields map to SIG QIDs we’ll flag them so they are searchable in our Compliance Console.

If Soojin wants I can draft the manifest template and a short import-run checklist (2–3 bullets) to attach.

—Rishi
Director, Platform Security | Redwood Inference

Hi Julia —

Thanks — attached are the quick artifacts you asked for:
- redwood_whistic_field_map_v1.csv (first 3 sample rows included) — column A is your field id, column B is our canonical name, column C is a suggested transformation (lowercase/trim).
- s3-presign-playbook.md — includes the manifest template, sample presign request, and instructions for scoping uploads to a customer prefix. TTL set to 24 hours by default; we can extend to 48 hours if legal confirms.

I’ve also created a one-off presign batch scoped to /acme-prod/whistic-import/ and generated 12 presigns (24h TTL) for john.doe@acme-soft.com. You should receive the upload links in a separate email from uploads@redwood.com; please confirm after upload and then post manifest_signed.json into the same prefix so we can validate checksums.

Import window: We’ll be in staging at 10:00 AM PT on Thursday for the dry-run — please confirm if you still prefer 10:00 AM. If John needs to be on the call, add him — otherwise security@acme-soft.com is fine.

Samplish excerpt of manifest template (manifest_signed.json):
{
  "uploaded_by": "john.doe@acme-soft.com",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-14T11:02:00Z",
  "files": [
    {"path": "evidence/whistic/sig_qid_47_design.pdf", "sha256": "<sha256>", "size": 51234}
  ],
  "signature": "--base64-signer--"
}

If that all looks good I’ll confirm the staging import and we’ll run the dry-run and final import Thursday.

Best,
Soojin Lee
